source_review.notes: Reviewed Pugh's primary sequential and concurrent skip-list papers, Herlihy-Wing linearizability, Fraser's primary lock-freedom report, current Java SE 26 ConcurrentSkipListMap/ConcurrentNavigableMap contracts, and current official RocksDB InlineSkipList/MemTable sources. All eight final destinations returned HTTP 200. Current library claims are limited to documented API/source behavior and historical performance is not generalized.

evidence: Checked comparator order/equivalence, levels L_i, tower height, geometric promotion, predecessor/successor windows, lifecycle states, histories, and evidence variables.
Checked that level-0 membership, auxiliary indexes, full publication, logical deletion, unlink, retirement, and reclamation are distinct.
Checked linearizable point operations, weak traversal, snapshot consistency, and progress classes remain separate contracts.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The notation supports both lazy lock-based and nonblocking proof templates without claiming one universal concrete representation.

evidence: Recomputed deterministic heights for keys 1..15: level widths 15,7,3,1 and tower subsets at each level.
Recomputed search for 11 advances through 8 and 10, yielding predecessor 10 and two forward hops; 16 is absent; range 5..10 contains six keys.
Recomputed E[height]=1/(1-p): 2 at p=1/2 and 4/3 at p=1/4; 800,000 nodes imply about 1,066,667 expected pointer slots before overhead.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Expected height and search claims are distribution/model statements; no actual memory, latency, or throughput value is presented as measured.

evidence: Verified geometric tail-sum derivation E[h]=sum p^j=1/(1-p) for uncapped independent promotion.
Verified top-down search preserves strict progress and predecessor/target bracketing while higher levels remain ordered subsequences.
Verified one chosen publication event defines insertion membership and one mark can define deletion while later index installation/unlinking remains auxiliary cleanup.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Proof conclusions are explicitly conditioned on validation, reader interpretation, target memory ordering, stable comparator behavior, and safe node lifetime.

evidence: Reviewed empty/head/tail, all-height-one, maximum-height, duplicate keys, repeated predecessor locks, stale windows, partial towers, marked nodes, reinsertion, and head-height retention.
Reviewed comparator failure/reentry/mutation, same-key insert/delete races, failed CAS, helper races, stalled owners, ABA, GC/native lifetime, clear/close/freeze, and allocation failure.
Reviewed weak ascending/descending ranges, atomic snapshot, size disagreement, adversarial height/key skew, unbounded scans, retained nodes, memory pressure, and hostile callbacks.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Operational bounds cover height, entries/bytes, retries/help, comparator work, range length/output, snapshot work, retired memory, freeze/close waits, and diagnostics.

evidence: The executable checks strict ordering of all four levels, exact level-0 membership, and every higher level as a subset of its predecessor.
The deterministic height rule produces consecutive tower levels without holes and exact search/range/predecessor outcomes.
Chapter invariants cover comparator stability, unique base membership, window validation, publication/mark interpretation, eventual/tolerated unlink, metadata semantics, and reclamation.
invariant_checking.notes: The topology model contains no mutation state and therefore does not verify a concurrent insertion, removal, mark, helper, or lifetime implementation.

evidence: Reviewed search proof from safely published head through right/down invariants to operation-specific presence/absence observations.
Reviewed lazy insertion from private initialization through deduplicated locks, adjacency/mark validation, link publication, chosen membership event, and exact cleanup.
Reviewed removal marking, physical helping/unlink, ABA/reclamation, blocking/optimistic/lock-free/wait-free progress obligations, range semantics, and all exercise solutions.
proof_review.notes: The module offers conditional proof templates; it does not declare an unspecified skip-list algorithm correct or transfer an insertion-only arena proof to delete-capable maps.

evidence: Expected logarithmic behavior and pointer counts are labeled probabilistic expectations with independence/cap assumptions.
Membership and deletion arguments require an implementation to choose and prove its exact event and reader interpretation.
Lock-free, wait-free, weak-iterator, race-tool, model, and benchmark claims are explicitly bounded to their definitions/evidence.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No deterministic latency, fairness, starvation freedom, snapshot atomicity, memory safety, or scalability follows merely from the skip-list shape or lack of mutexes.

evidence: The standard-library-only Python topology model passed exact eleven-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the repository verifier.
It emits evidence=finite_skip_list_topology_model and reproduces exact levels, searches, predecessor, range, hops, order, and subset invariants.
All eight final external destinations returned HTTP 200 and all repository-local links passed chapter validation.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No randomized distribution sample, runtime threads, locks/CAS, memory ordering, concurrent mutation, mark/unlink, ABA/reclamation, progress, callback/fault, range-overlap, or performance experiment was run.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter derives topology and probability first, separates base membership from upper indexes, then develops search, lazy and nonblocking updates, deletion/reclamation, range/size contracts, height generation, layout, evidence, and production specialization.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed comparator/key stability, duplicate lock handling, validation, publication ordering, mark/unlink/help, exact progress terminology, range/snapshot/size APIs, RNG and height bounds, arena specialization, lifecycle, memory telemetry, adversarial tests, and point/range benchmarks.

pedagogical_review.notes: The dense review supports retrieval; a reproducible topology model anchors structure; ten varied examples cover probability, locking, publication, validation, deletion, progress, ranges, ABA, memtables, and benchmarking; five progressive exercises have complete model answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/official-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, Pugh, Herlihy/Wing, Fraser, Oracle, RocksDB, probability, concurrency, storage-engine, security, performance, reliability, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and topology model prove neither a concrete concurrent skip list, random-height distribution in production, deterministic complexity, runtime threads/locks/CAS, target memory ordering, arbitrary histories/interleavings, comparator/callback safety, deletion/ABA/reclamation correctness, lock-free or wait-free progress, atomic range snapshots, production memory/latency/throughput/cache/NUMA behavior, certification, nor deployment fitness.
